challenges.title: Which certification category has the most films?
challenges.context: The marketing team wants to know which MPAA certification (like PG, R) appears most often in the films database, so they can target ads to the most popular rating category.

instructions.description: Write a SELECT statement that retrieves the certification column and a count of films, aliased as film_count.
instructions.hint: Use COUNT(*) to count rows per certification.

instructions.description: Add a GROUP BY clause to group the films by certification.
instructions.hint: Every non-aggregate column in SELECT must appear in GROUP BY.

instructions.description: Add an ORDER BY clause to sort the groups by film_count in descending order.
Add a LIMIT 1 to keep only the top certification.

challenges.starter_code:
-- Write your SQL query here
-- Tables available: films, people, reviews, roles

SELECT certification, COUNT(*) AS film_count
FROM films
-- Finish the query
challenges.solution_code:
SELECT certification, COUNT(*) AS film_count
FROM films
GROUP BY certification
ORDER BY film_count DESC
LIMIT 1;
challenges.output_description: The certification 'R' appears most frequently (2345 films) in the database.
hints: Group by certification first, then count.
Use ORDER BY with DESC to see the highest count at the top.
challenges.learning_outcome: Proves ability to use GROUP BY to summarize data and ORDER BY to rank groups.

challenges.title: Which release years have more than 50 films?
challenges.context: The archive team wants to identify 'boom years' in film production — years where more than 50 films were released in the database.

instructions.description: Write a query that selects release_year and a count of films, aliased as num_films.
instructions.hint: Use COUNT(*) to count films per year.

instructions.description: Add a GROUP BY clause to group by release_year.
instructions.hint: The column release_year must appear in GROUP BY.

instructions.description: Add a HAVING clause to keep only groups where num_films > 50.
instructions.hint: HAVING filters after grouping, unlike WHERE.

instructions.description: Order the results by release_year ascending to see the chronology.

challenges.starter_code:
-- Write your SQL query here
-- Tables available: films, people, reviews, roles

SELECT release_year, COUNT(*) AS num_films
FROM films
-- Complete the rest
challenges.solution_code:
SELECT release_year, COUNT(*) AS num_films
FROM films
GROUP BY release_year
HAVING COUNT(*) > 50
ORDER BY release_year;
challenges.output_description: Three years (2005, 2006, 2007) each had more than 50 films in the database.
hints: Think about the order: GROUP BY then HAVING then ORDER BY.
You need to use the aggregate COUNT(*) inside the HAVING clause.
challenges.learning_outcome: Proves ability to use HAVING to filter grouped results based on aggregate conditions.

challenges.title: List big-budget US films released after 2000
challenges.context: A producer wants a list of all US films made after the year 2000 with a budget exceeding 100 million dollars, for a potential investment study.

instructions.description: Write a query that selects title, release_year, and budget from the films table.
Add a WHERE clause to filter for rows where country equals 'USA'.
instructions.hint: String values must be enclosed in single quotes.

instructions.description: Extend the WHERE clause with AND to require release_year > 2000.
Add another AND condition so that budget > 100000000.

challenges.starter_code:
-- Write your SQL query here
-- Tables available: films

SELECT title, release_year, budget
FROM films
-- Add filtering
challenges.solution_code:
SELECT title, release_year, budget
FROM films
WHERE country = 'USA'
  AND release_year > 2000
  AND budget > 100000000;
challenges.output_description: Three US films met the criteria: Avatar, The Dark Knight, and Transformers.
hints: Use single quotes for the string 'USA'.
Combine conditions with AND, not commas.
challenges.learning_outcome: Proves ability to filter rows using WHERE with multiple AND conditions and proper string quoting.

challenges.title: What are the key statistics of all films?
challenges.context: The analytics team needs a quick summary of the films database: total number of films, the range of release years, average duration, and total combined budget.

instructions.description: Write a query that uses COUNT(*) to count all films, aliased as total_films.
instructions.hint: COUNT(*) returns the number of rows.

instructions.description: Add MIN(release_year) as earliest and MAX(release_year) as latest to find the year range.
instructions.hint: MIN and MAX work on numeric and date columns.

instructions.description: Add AVG(duration) as avg_duration to get the mean film length.
instructions.hint: AVG ignores NULLs; round the result with ROUND(…, 2).

instructions.description: Add SUM(budget) as total_budget to see the combined spending.
instructions.hint: SUM adds all non‑NULL budget values.

challenges.starter_code:
-- Write your SQL query here
-- Tables available: films

SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS total_films,
  -- Add more aggregate functions
FROM films;
challenges.solution_code:
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS total_films,
  MIN(release_year) AS earliest,
  MAX(release_year) AS latest,
  ROUND(AVG(duration), 2) AS avg_duration,
  SUM(budget) AS total_budget
FROM films;
challenges.output_description: The films database spans from 1916 to 2016, contains 4968 films with an average duration of 107.32 minutes, and a total budget of over 181 billion.
hints: Multiple aggregate functions can be used in a single SELECT.
Use ROUND() to control decimal places in the average.
challenges.learning_outcome: Proves ability to apply multiple aggregate functions together to summarize a dataset.
